# Draft:Madhya Pradesh Patwari Sangh, Bhopal

Madhya Pradesh Patwari Sangh, Bhopal is an association representing patwaris (village revenue officers) in the Indian state of Madhya Pradesh. The organisation works on matters related to service conditions, administrative responsibilities, and professional issues concerning patwaris. Its headquarters is located in Bhopal, the capital of Madhya Pradesh.
History
The Madhya Pradesh Patwari Sangh was formed to provide a collective platform for patwaris to raise administrative and service-related issues before government authorities. Over the years, the association has submitted memoranda and representations to the state administration on issues related to duties, workload, and service conditions. Some of these activities have been reported by independent regional newspapers.
Objectives
The objectives of the Madhya Pradesh Patwari Sangh include:
* Representing service-related and professional concerns of patwaris in Madhya Pradesh.
* Engaging with government departments on administrative and revenue-related duties.
* Facilitating coordination among patwaris at state and district levels.
Activities
The Madhya Pradesh Patwari Sangh has been involved in organisational activities such as meetings, submission of memoranda, and collective actions by its members.
In several districts, units of the Patwari Sangh have organised protests and collective leave to raise demands related to reinstatement of suspended patwaris and changes in work assignments, which have been reported by regional newspapers.
At the same time, the association has also issued official communications requesting the withdrawal of certain non-revenue duties assigned to patwaris, including duties related to voter list preparation.
Leadership
The association is led by a state-level committee. As of the current term, Upendra Singh Baghel serves as the president of the Madhya Pradesh Patwari Sangh, Bhopal.
Organisational structure
The Madhya Pradesh Patwari Sangh operates through office-bearers at the state and district levels. Office-bearers are selected according to the internal rules of the organisation. District-level units coordinate with the state body to address professional and administrative issues faced by patwaris.
